title: Fine-Grained Role Composition & Scope Binding for RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: RBAC v1 has served us for coarse-grained admin roles but does not map well to multi-tenant resource hierarchies, dedicated capacity controls, or scoped delegated admin needs. Goal: define a role model that supports composable role expressions (capability sets), explicit scope binding to hierarchical resources (org/team/project/cluster), and a machine-readable permissions matrix that can be validated at runtime and audited. This ticket captures the design, trade-offs, and implementation plan for the canonical role model used by RBAC v2.
progress_updates: 2025-03-12: Kickoff meeting with Security, Platform, and Console; agreed on composable role primitives vs monolithic role blobs.
2025-03-14: Narrowed scope binding semantics: explicit allow list for scope propagation; no implicit grant through parent unless 'inherit' flag set on role binding.
2025-03-17: Proof-of-concept policy evaluator implemented that resolves composed roles into a flattened permission set (link to GH PR below).
2025-03-20: UX workshop with Console team to map role bindings to rollout UI; decided to surface effective permissions and audit trail in role binding details.
decisions: Adopt a small set of capability atoms (read, write, manage, deploy, monitor, billing) and build composite roles by unioning atoms.

Scope binding model: resource identifiers are hierarchical (org:team:project:resource). RoleBinding attaches Role to a principal + explicit scope resource. By default inheritance=false; an 'inherit:true' optional flag is supported for admin roles.
Permission matrix will be canonical JSON documents stored in the control plane and versioned; runtime will cache evaluated flattened sets.
Audit log will record RoleBinding changes, effective permission evaluations for privileged API calls, and break-glass emergency grants.
SSO/SAML mapping: external groups map to RoleBindings; we will support attribute-based mapping and explicit group-to-role mappings to avoid privilege explosion.
tradeoffs: Explicit inheritance=false by default reduces accidental scope leakage but requires more RoleBindings for nested management. Operational cost vs safety tradeoff acknowledged.
Storing canonical permission matrices increases control-plane storage but simplifies evaluation and enables offline reviews; alternative of eval-on-the-fly rejected due to auditability concerns.
Composable atoms make reasoning easier but may produce many small roles; will ship a set of curated composite roles for common patterns (project-admin, billing-reader, runtime-deployer).
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by Security and Platform leads.
Policy evaluator PR merged with unit tests covering inheritance, deny/allow precedence, and composite roles.
Console surfaces role binding UI that shows effective permissions and provenance link to audit entries.
E2E tests demonstrating SSO group->RoleBinding flows and emergency break-glass provisioning with audit entries.
Performance benchmark showing permission evaluation <2ms p50 for cached flattening in serving runtime under 2000 concurrent requests.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Design+Spec): Finalize atom set and canonical permission schema; publish JSON schema for role documents.
Phase 2 (Control Plane): Add storage for versioned permission matrices; implement Role and RoleBinding APIs; expose Change events to audit log service.
Phase 3 (Runtime): Integrate cached evaluator into request path; add fallback to control plane for uncached entries; measure latency and tune cache TTLs.
Phase 4 (Console+SSO): UX for creating RoleBindings, mapping SAML groups, and showing effective permissions; add tests for group mapping edge cases.
Phase 5 (Rollout): Beta for internal teams, iterate on curated composite roles, then gradual rollout to customers with migration tooling.
test_plan: Unit tests: role composition algebra, inheritance semantics, deny precedence, conflict resolution.
Integration tests: SAML group mapping -> RoleBinding -> permission check across org/team/project boundaries.
Load tests: evaluate permission check latency at 2k qps with 50k cached bindings; measure CPU and memory overhead.
Audit tests: verify audit events emitted for Role/RoleBinding changes, emergency grants, and evaluated permission snapshots for critical API calls.
notes_and_links: Incident context: INC-2024-09: accidental tenant-wide admin created via inherited binding — motivates default inheritance=false and explicit 'inherit' opt-in.
Design reference: previous RBAC discussions: ENG-41327 and ENG-52034; this ticket consolidates and diverges in explicit composition and audit snapshots.
